what_its_for: Chlorthalidone is a water pill (diuretic) used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and fluid buildup (edema) caused by heart failure, kidney problems, or liver disease. Lowering high blood pressure helps prevent strokes, heart attacks, and kidney problems.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, usually once a day in the morning with or without food. Taking it in the morning helps prevent you from needing to urinate during the night. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first, even if you feel fine.
dosing: Your doctor will prescribe the dose that is right for you. For high blood pressure, the usual starting dose is 12.5 to 25 mg once daily. For fluid buildup, doses may range from 50 to 100 mg once daily or every other day. Never change your dose on your own. Always follow your doctor's instructions.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is the same day. If it is already the next day, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Dispose of unused or expired medicine safely — ask your pharmacist how.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking large amounts of alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Avoid standing up too quickly from a sitting or lying position to reduce the risk of dizziness or fainting. Limit foods very high in salt, as excess salt can reduce how well this medicine works. Be careful in hot weather or during exercise, as you may lose more fluids and become dehydrated. Talk to your doctor before using potassium supplements or salt substitutes containing potassium.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you experience: severe dizziness, lightheadedness, or fainting; muscle cramps, weakness, or irregular heartbeat (signs of low potassium); little or no urination; dry mouth, extreme thirst, or confusion (signs of dehydration); signs of an allergic reaction such as rash, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing; unusual bruising or bleeding; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or vision changes or eye pain.
when_it_works: You may start urinating more frequently within the first few hours of taking your first dose. However, it may take 2 to 4 weeks of regular use to see the full benefit for blood pressure control. Keep taking your medicine even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to the effects of this medicine, especially dizziness and low blood pressure. Rise slowly from sitting or lying positions. Pregnant women: This medicine is generally not recommended during pregnancy. Talk to your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Breastfeeding mothers: Chlorthalidone may pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. People with diabetes: This medicine may raise your blood sugar levels. Monitor your blood sugar more closely and tell your doctor if you notice any changes. People with gout: This medicine may raise uric acid levels and trigger gout attacks. Inform your doctor if you have a history of gout. People with kidney or liver disease: Dose adjustments may be needed. Your doctor will monitor you closely.
